items.title: Marshall Lawrence Interview, 1960-06-28
items.q: He played trumpet with us for a while, with our little bands.

ctx.x: Oh, I guess so. I knew him, I went to school on him. I went to night school. He couldn't read. You know that man, he could play an instrument and he couldn't read. You know, when we first started, before I started to play with Dijon, well, we asked him to teach us. So he said, all right. And when we get a piece of music, well, we were expecting him to help us divide the music. You know, he said, go ahead and I'll come in. But he couldn't read, you see. He could play anything you play. Anything you hear, he could…
Well, I heard of him as a trombone player.
